finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id calls authorize() without await or return, so the delete at line 21 runs regardless of the grant check result. Any caller, including an anonymous one with no session user, can delete any report.
finding.source: E1: DELETE /reports/:id (server.js:18), req.params.id and req.user from session (server.js:4-5)

trace.note: Loads report by req.params.id with no null check
authorize(req.user,'delete',report) called without await/return; returns pending promise; any throw becomes an unhandled rejection
db.reports.remove(report.id) executes before grant lookup resolves
db.grants lookup; user.id throws if req.user undefined, rejecting the unawaited promise
Sibling PUT handler uses await authorize(...), showing the omission is a bug

finding.guards_checked: authorize() check at server.js:9-16 is correct but its result and rejection are discarded; no null check on report; no await/return at server.js:20; no error handling around the call. Unhandled rejection on Node 15+ can terminate the process.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. The authorize() check at server.js:9-16 exists and throws on a missing grant, but its result is discarded because the call at server.js:20 is a bare statement with no await or return. Nothing else sits between the request and db.reports.remove at server.js:21, which runs in the same synchronous tick as the unawaited call. The PUT handler at server.js:27 awaits authorize(), so the omission is specific to DELETE.
verdict.reason: At server.js:20 authorize() is called without await, so the removal at server.js:21 runs whatever the grant lookup returns, and the only guard (server.js:11-14) throws into a discarded promise. Every trace line checks out (19, 20, 21, 22, 10, 27). The one caveat is that server.js:5 reads req.session.user, so an anonymous request needs session middleware (not in this file) to supply a session object; with a standard session middleware it does, and the delete still runs for any caller.
